Diffraction-ready average R-3m B4C model in the conventional hexagonal setting. The atomic coordinates follow the Clark-Hoard/JCPDS average structure; split B/C occupancy on the polar icosahedral site gives exactly B36C9 in the cell. The lattice parameters a=5.601(1) A and c=12.087(5) A are the ambient sample values reported by Somayazulu et al. in the official supplement and give V=328.383 A^3, consistent with the fixed 328.4 A^3 EOS reference volume. Structure references: Clark and Hoard, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 65, 2115-2119 (1943), doi:10.1021/ja01251a026; Somayazulu et al. (2023), doi:10.1098/rsta.2022.0331; JCPDS/PDF 6-0555. PhaseSmith can expand the five asymmetric sites to calculate powder reflections and intensities.

<details markdown="1">
<summary>Thermal equation choices</summary>

- **Debye temperature law:** integrated\_gruneisen

</details>

Third-order Birch-Murnaghan reference isotherm plus Mie-Gruneisen-Debye thermal pressure. The room-temperature quench-data fit gives K0=221(2) GPa and K0'=3.3(1) with V0=328.4 A^3 fixed; those three reference parameters were then fixed in the P-V-T fit. The official supplement defines T0=298 K, theta0=1425 K, n=5 atoms per B4C formula unit, gamma(V)=gamma0\*(V/V0)^q, and theta(V)=theta0\*exp\[(gamma0-gamma(V))/q\]. With a=1, the paper's generalized Tange relation reduces exactly to this integrated constant-q MGD model. The final article reports gamma0=0.8 fixed and q=2.1 varied. At the 41 heated supplementary points' printed V and T, the published parameterization gives a pressure RMSE of 1.39 GPa and chi-squared per observation of 0.961. A Peritheos P-V-T errors-in-variables refit with gamma0 fixed gives q=1.050(519), so it does not independently recover q=2.1; details and the primary-data transcription are in docs/literature-reproductions.md. The average disordered R-3m structure is diffraction-ready and is reported stable over the experimental range.

Parameter covariance is not supplied.

<details markdown="1">
<summary>Thermal equation choices</summary>

- **Thermal expansion law:** linear\_temperature
- **Reference volume law:** berman

</details>

The paper calls this the Berman P-V-T fit. EosFit7 implements the Berman reference volume as the truncated quadratic V0(T)=V0\*\[1+alpha0\*(T-Tr)+0.5\*alpha1\*(T-Tr)^2\], with K0(T)=K0+dK0/dT\*(T-Tr). EosFit7c varied alpha0=1.94(16)e-5 K^-1 and dK0/dT=-0.008(3) GPa/K while alpha1=0.0573e-8 K^-2 and the 300 K BM3 parameters were fixed. The article's displayed exponential-integral equation instead describes EosFit's Fei-style exact integration and is inconsistent with its Berman label. The implied BM3 K0''=-0.0166 GPa^-1 is derived rather than an independent parameter. Reproduction diagnostics compare both EosFit effective-variance and Peritheos errors-in-variables objectives.

Parameter covariance is not supplied.

<details markdown="1">
<summary>Thermal equation choices</summary>

- **Thermal expansion law:** linear\_temperature
- **Reference volume law:** berman

</details>

Opt-in refit of the public rounded dataset, not a parameter set published by Somayazulu et al. The official EosFit7c 7.60 executable refined alpha0 and dK0/dT against the 41 heated rows using all reported P, V, and T sigmas; reference-isotherm parameters, Tr, and alpha1 were fixed. The covariance matrix is reconstructed from EosFit's rounded standard errors and -95.8% printed correlation after its W-CHI^2 rescaling. Uncertainty in the fixed reference-isotherm parameters was not propagated. The unchanged published record b4c\_somayazulu\_2023\_berman\_2 remains the literature parameterization.

Parameter covariance is supplied in the complete EOSMAT source.
